chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Does a man perform Hajj on behalf of a woman, and does a woman perform Hajj on behalf of a man?' He said: 'There is no harm in it.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: 'These two reports, even if they occurred in two years, indicate the permissibility of a woman performing Hajj on behalf of a man in all cases. However, it is preferable to specify them for a woman who has already performed her obligatory Hajj (Hajjat al-Islam), because if she were a newborn infant, it would not be valid for her to perform Hajj on behalf of a man, which indicates this ruling.'

key_terms.حَجَّةَ الإِسْلَام: The first obligatory pilgrimage, known as Hajjat al-Islam

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a woman to perform Hajj on behalf of a man in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records the permissibility of reciprocal Hajj representation, but Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari introduces a critical juristic nuance: this mutual validity is specifically restricted to a woman who has already performed her own obligatory Hajj. He argues that if she has not yet fulfilled her duty, she cannot represent a man, as the logic of representation implies the agent is free from their own primary obligation, unlike a newborn who is exempt entirely.
